law: G4 (owner plan 2026-11-13): fixed workflows run as machine contracts against the built wheel in a disposable workspace with a local bare origin. Measures per journey: approvals (owner consents, exact baseline) and blocked (every Kit step ends PASS, PLANNED or AWAITING_APPROVAL; baseline 0). A worse measure fails CI. Offline the journeys stop at the GitHub boundary (work finish as dry run); J2 emulates merge and post-merge closeout with git and handoff steps. Approvals count signed executions and steps with effects beyond none/fetch/push/network_read (owner decision 2026-11-13); a release run asks for consent only through a signed execution. J4 runs a release run in the release fixture, whose remotes the runner confines to the run's temporary root; it declares one interruption (the origin refuses B4's push), the only step that may end BLOCKED, and stops at the signed resume gate, whose execution is the GitHub part. J5 runs release run without summary lines in the curated variant of the release fixture and checks the prepared release section line by line (assert section). J6 starts without a project: agentic-kit init creates it in the empty run root of the init fixture, run steps name their working directory (cwd) inside the run root, and release run prepares the first release (no previous v* tag) up to the B4 gate.

journeys.title: Start work, change a file, finish

machine.covers: J1: work start from main, one changed file, work finish plans commit, push, PR, merge and closeout without a BLOCKED step

journeys.title: Adopt a Kit release, then a release with only that adoption

machine.covers: J2 (V1, V6, V11): in a curated workspace, a signed kit update installs real wheels from a loopback index and writes the adoption line (K4); work finish plans to publish it; after the merge the release is ready with only that line and without a BLOCKED step. Merge and post-merge closeout run as git and handoff steps until the live run covers the GitHub part; the post-merge handoff refresh leaves no tracked change (observed in run 0082), which the contract asserts.
J3 (V8): a change committed by hand on the work branch; work finish without --path plans to publish the existing commit (K1) without a BLOCKED step

journeys.title: Release interrupted inside B4, then resumed

interruption.cause: the origin refuses the push of the release branch (push URL set to a missing path), so B4 stops after its release commit

machine.covers: J4 (K7): a release run plans B4 and executes it signed; the origin refuses the push, so B4 stops after the release commit with nothing on the origin. The next plan run offers the signed K7 resume gate (publish the existing commits with work finish) instead of blocking with changed-paths-drift, without a GitHub call and without changing the worktree.

run: Add diagnostics with regression tests, verified release metadata and successor handoff evidence

journeys.title: Curated release with exactly one line

machine.covers: J5 (K8, V1): a curated workspace whose merged PR left exactly one Unreleased line runs release run without summary lines, as the Kit's own release now does. It reaches the B4 gate without a BLOCKED step; the prepared release section carries exactly that line and Unreleased is empty. Offline the run stops at the B4 gate, whose signed execution is the GitHub part.

journeys.title: From init to the first release

machine.covers: J6 (KIT-GF-118): agentic-kit init creates the project and its external operating layer in an empty run root; the journey adds the local bare origin and pushes, as init --github does on GitHub. The generated workspace has publication none and receives a CI update without a hand tag or hand configuration. release run then prepares the first release: no previous v* tag, notes from the root commit with the init and adoption commits listed as direct commits, and the B4 gate carries first_release. It reaches the B4 gate without a BLOCKED step; offline the run stops there, whose signed execution is the GitHub part.
